title: Data-center copper interconnect energy ceiling
bottleneck: Moving data over copper at 100+ Gbps per lane costs growing energy per bit as equalization, retimers, and error correction multiply; copper reach shrinks with each speed generation, forcing power-hungry retimers every few meters. At rack and row scale, interconnect energy rivals compute energy for AI training. Physics offers no relief: loss per meter rises with frequency.
why_it_blocks: Interconnect energy sets a floor under AI training cost and data-center power: even free compute couldn't make training cheap if moving the data costs more. Scaling to larger GPU clusters hits a wall where the network, not the chips, dominates power and cost.
current_state: 224 Gbps SerDes and linear pluggable optics extend copper's life, while co-packaged optics and optical circuit switching promise relief. Copper remains dominant, with its energy ceiling approaching.
